text:
sophia: Hey @kevin-customer — following up on your ticket. You mentioned the embed backfill started throwing errors around yesterday evening and that throughput dropped to near zero. Can you paste the exact error + one example request payload? :eyes:

kevin-customer: throwing the error here — indexer logs show this on every batch:```ERROR indexer batch 2024-11-02T19:22:13Z: vector dim 1536 != expected 1024, rejecting record id=usr_12345
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/indexer/worker.py", line 213, in process_batch
    assert vec.shape[0] == expected_dim
AssertionError```

kevin-customer: sample request payload we send to /v1/embeddings (python):```payload = {
  "model": "open-embedder-v2",
  "input": [ ... ],
  "batch_size": 128
}```We haven't changed our code; last successful backfill was 11/01 03:14 UTC.

ashok: thanks — two quick Qs: did you pin the embedding model previously (e.g., open-embedder-v1) and then switch to v2? v2 _is_ 1536 dim, v1 was 1024. Also any quantization/adapter in your client?

kevin-customer: we didn't intentionally switch. Our infra team upgraded a pip dep on Nov 1 but didn't think it would change model selection. We do call the Redwood API with model string from config: sometimes it's dynamic. Could the API have started returning a different default?

maria: @ashok to confirm, but last rollout to the hosted embeddings catalog included an alias change: alias "recommended-embed" now points to open-embedder-v2 (1536). We had a migration note but might have missed some customers using alias instead of fixed model id. Ops posted a changelog #release-notes earlier.

daniel: ok that explains mismatch — indexer expects 1024 vectors (schema migration from initial product launch). Two possible paths: 1) re-run backfill using the new model so DB schema updates to 1536, or 2) convert vectors on ingest (pad/truncate) — but padding is lossy and will break search quality.

kevin-customer: customer-facing issue here: backfill is stuck and they're seeing a billing surge because client retries on rejects. We need a mitigation ASAP.

ashok: mitigation plan I suggest: temporary rollback the alias to v1 for requests originating from kevin-customer's API key (scope-specific alias) so their backfill can finish while we plan proper migration. Steps: 1) identify API key(s) used, 2) set alias mapping override for those keys, 3) run a small dry run backfill to sanity-check.

sophia: kevin, can you DM the API key(s) or paste them here privately? If you prefer we can do a per-tenant override.

kevin-customer: DMed the key. Also attaching small failing record: id usr_99999 with payload:```{"id":"usr_99999","text":"profile bio...","embedding_dims":1536}```

indexer-bot: Alert: 1200 rejects in the last hour for tenant kevin-orga due to dim mismatch. Current reject rate 98%.

maria: I can do the alias override for that key now, will flip to open-embedder-v1 for kevin-orga for the next 1 hour. That should allow their restart to proceed.

ops-bot: deploy requested by maria — change alias mapping for api_key=k-cust-XXXXX -> open-embedder-v1 (temporal override). CI check OK.

maria: override applied. please try restarting one worker at a time and watch for new rejects.

kevin-customer: restarting backfill with batch_size=64 concurrency=8 now. Will report if rejects persist.

kevin-customer: update after 7 minutes — rejects dropped to 0, throughput ~1200 recs/min, but observed an unexpected latency increase from 220ms -> 420ms per call. Also billing shows a small spike due to retries earlier.

daniel: latency jump likely from smaller batch size and extra client-side retries earlier. For long-term, we need schema migration: choose target dim (1536) and migrate data (re-embed old docs) or support multi-dim index variants. Both require a planned backfill.

ashok: recommendation: we roll a migration plan:
- Phase 1 (short-term): per-tenant alias fixes + backfill with pinned model, monitor cost and latency.
- Phase 2 (migration): schedule off-hours migration to 1536 for tenants who opt in. Provide tools: reindex script with checkpointing and per-shard parallelism.

maria: I'll open a private PR with an operator script (reindexer) that supports: `--batch-size`, `--concurrency`, `--checkpoint-key`, `--dry-run`. Dan will wire it into the ops runbook.

kevin-customer: thanks. For transparency their legal/compliance teams want an estimate of how long a full backfill for 12M objects would take and cost delta. Any rough numbers?

daniel: ballpark: with current infra, re-embedding 12M docs at 1200 recs/min ~ 10k min ~ 170 hours if single-threaded. With concurrency=8 across multiple workers you can bring it down to ~22 hours. Token costs depend on model: v1 cost $0.0004/req, v2 $0.0007/req — so incremental embedding cost ~ 12M*(0.0003) = ~$3.6k for full re-embed. These are approximate.

ashok: also remind customer to consider quality regression tests — we should run a small eval set before and after to validate search recall. Redwood Optimize can run the eval and surface delta.

maria: created issue INF-2483 with the reindex script attached and scheduled a runbook meeting 2024-11-04 15:00 UTC. I set owner=daniel, oncall=ashok.

kevin-customer: appreciated. Quick followups: 1) can you prevent future alias flips from affecting customers using ambiguous model strings? 2) can you give us a way to fail fast on dim mismatch instead of retrying until billing spikes?

ashok: 1) we're adding per-tenant alias overrides and will add a warning banner when alias changes globally (next deploy). 2) we can expose a strict_dim_check header `X-Redwood-Strict-Dim: true|false`. If set true, API will return 400 on mismatches (no retries). Will aim for a small patch within 48 hours.

sophia: tagging this as escalated -> high priority. kevin, I'll follow with JIRA links and the PRs once they land. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Deploy complete (alias rollback for k-cust-XXXXX).

maria: after-action items:
- Confirm billing credit for retry surge (billing team) [owner: sophia]
- Publish reindexer runbook + dry-run checklist [owner: daniel]
- Add API header for strict dim check [owner: ashok]
- Notify customers using `recommended-embed` alias about potential dim change and recommended steps [owner: product]

kevin-customer: perfect. We'll schedule migration window and run small eval before full backfill. Thanks all.

sophia: closing thread once billing is confirmed and PRs merged.
